## TL;DR

The E2 test in `src/ui-app/tests/easter-eggs-1026.test.ts` depended on the host machine. `resolveServeHost(undefined)` calls `detectTailscaleIPv4()`, which runs `tailscale ip -4`, so any machine with Tailscale running got `0.0.0.0` and failed the `127.0.0.1` assertion. I stubbed `detectTailscaleIPv4` at file level and made E2 set its return value per case. The test now covers the undetected default, the Tailscale-detected default, and explicit `--host` winning in both states. No production code changed. The file passes 8/8 on this machine, which has Tailscale running and reports `100.106.252.73` from `tailscale ip -4`.

## Work and rationale

The fix stays in the test. `resolveServeHost` is intentional (its doc comment in `src/commands/serve.ts` explains why the default flips to `0.0.0.0` on a tailnet), so the code under test is correct and only the test's assumption was wrong.

I used `vi.mock("../../core/tailscale.js", ...)` with `importOriginal` and a spread, the same idiom the other tests in `src/ui-app/tests/` use. The spread keeps `ensureTailscaleHttps` real, since `serve.ts` imports it from the same module. The default is `vi.fn(() => null)`, so the file starts in the undetected state. Only E2 calls `resolveServeHost`, so a file-level mock does not affect the other seven tests.

Inside E2 each case sets the mock explicitly with `mockReturnValue`:

- Undetected: `resolveServeHost(undefined)` returns `{ host: "127.0.0.1", tailscaleDetected: false }`.
- Detected (`100.64.0.7`): returns `{ host: "0.0.0.0", tailscaleDetected: true, tailscaleIP }`, using `toEqual` so the shape is checked, not just `host`.
- Explicit `--host`: `127.0.0.1` and `0.0.0.0` both return `tailscaleDetected: false` even while Tailscale is detected.

The existing banner assertions are unchanged. They already cover the `127.0.0.1 (localhost only)` text and the wide `0.0.0.0 (all interfaces` text with the `--host 127.0.0.1` hint. I kept them in the same test instead of splitting E2, so the test name and grouping stay as they were.

I used a module mock rather than the task's "spy on" option. `serve.ts` imports `detectTailscaleIPv4` as a named binding, and a module mock replaces that binding before the import resolves. I did not test `vi.spyOn` against this export.

## Approaches tried

I considered two other options before settling on the module mock:

1. Setting an environment variable or changing `PATH` so `tailscale` is absent. This depends on the shell environment, and it would not cover the detected case without also needing a fake binary that prints an IP. Rejected.
2. Spying on `child_process.spawnSync` to fake `tailscale ip -4`. This tests the implementation detail of how the IP is found, and `detectTailscaleIPv4` may use other calls. The task asks to stub `detectTailscaleIPv4` directly, so I did that.

The first attempt at running the file used a bare `bunx vitest run`. It failed on an unrelated file, `easter-eggs-1058-card-activity.test.ts`, with a `.vue` import-analysis error. That came from skipping the repo's own runner, not from my change. Running through `bun run test -- easter-eggs` (the wrapper AGENTS.md requires) gave 43/43 passing across 5 files.

## Challenges and blockers

I did not run the unmodified test on this machine to watch it fail. The baseline failure is inferred from the live output of `tailscale ip -4` here, which returns an IP, combined with the old assertion `resolveServeHost(undefined).host === "127.0.0.1"`. Re-running the old file would confirm it, but I did not do so.

`REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` passed every local step: format, lint, build, css-layers, theme-contrast, hardcoded-colors, rendered-contrast, bare-require, branch-artifacts and ui-smoke. The `tests` step was skipped because this runner sets `REPOOS_SKIP_TESTS=1` and the suite runs on the remote validation runner. I covered the affected tests with `bun run test -- easter-eggs` instead. That run is the local evidence, and the remote run is the authoritative one.

I did not verify the other tailnet machines or a real `tailscale` outage. The test stubs the function, so it does not check what `detectTailscaleIPv4` returns on a real machine. Real detection is not covered by E2. The sibling `src/ui-app/tests/tailscale-https.test.ts` also touches `core/tailscale.js`, but I did not read it closely, and I did not change it.

## Key learnings

- A test that calls a function reading host state (a binary on `PATH`, a running daemon) inherits that state. Stub at the module boundary the code imports from, not at the shell.
- `vi.spyOn` does not work on a named ESM export that a module has already bound. Use `vi.mock` with `importOriginal` and a spread so the rest of the module stays real.
- Put the mock default in the file header and set the per-case value inside each case with `mockReturnValue`. Then the cases don't depend on each other's order.
- Run the repo's own test wrapper (`bun run test`). A bare `vitest` call bypasses the Vue plugin config and gives misleading import errors on unrelated files.
